parole.significato: Friends, gang, guys, a group of friends.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yiddish חבֿרה (khevre), in turn from Hebrew חֶבְרָה (khevrá), which is a doublet. An apostrophe or geresh is usually used to disambiguate from meanings above.

parole.significato: booty, butt, buttocks (chiefly in speech by or with children)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yiddish טוסיק (tusik), from תּחת (tokhes, “butt”) + ־יק (-ik, diminutive suffix), the first part from Hebrew תַּחַת (tákhat, “bottom, underside”). Compare English tush.
Borrowed from Yiddish שלימיל (shlimil), which may be a reborrowing from Hebrew שלא מועיל or the proper name שלמיאל.
Borrowed from Yiddish תּכלית (takhles, “goal”) after being borrowed from the original Hebrew תַּכְלִית (takhlít, “purpose, aim”), which is a doublet.
